assessments.reasoning: The release-tagged parse.y file matched its digest. Lines 215–230 require full-length case-insensitive names and assign TF_WithoutRowid together with TF_NoVisibleRowid in one branch and TF_Strict in the other.

challenge.method: I traced the exact name length and case-insensitive comparisons in both 3.46.0 parser actions. I tested mixed-case options separately and together against the release amalgamation, plus the near-miss names ROWIDS and STRICTER. https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/releases/tag/version-3.46.0 I compiled the project’s 3.46.0 amalgamation with loadable extensions disabled and exercised only an in-memory database. The amalgamation’s sqlite3.c SHA3-256 matched the 3.46.0 release log. The executable reported source ID 96c92aba00c8375bc32fafcdf12429c58bd8aabfcadab6683e35bbb9cdebf19e. https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-3460000.zip
challenge.results: Mixed-case STRICT alone set the strict state with rowid present. Mixed-case WITHOUT ROWID alone set the without-rowid state with strict clear. Both orders set both states. The two near-miss names produced unknown-option errors. The parser actions identify the distinct constants directly.

limitations: This describes parser recognition and flag mapping at SQLite 3.46.0. The run checked exposed option states, and the exact internal constants were confirmed from the pinned code. Downstream validation and storage semantics are outside scope.
